exposure: Mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
Abnormal labor or pregnancy (APH, pre-eclampsia, obstructed labor, fetal distress, and mal-presentation)
Presence of meconium in the amniotic fluid
outcome: Adverse neonatal outcome (birth asphyxia, respiratory distress, birth trauma, hypothermia, meconium aspiration syndrome, neonatal intensive care admission, and neonatal death)
finding: The risk of adverse neonatal outcome was higher among babies born through cesarean section than those born via vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: The presence of meconium in the amniotic fluid increased the risk of adverse neonatal outcomes for babies delivered via cesarean section.
